links.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd edition: Chapter 19, Keeping Time, Scheduling Tasks, and Launching Programs
links.why: The course textbook's own chapter, free online: the time and datetime modules, subprocess, the stopwatch and countdown projects, and the practice questions.

links.title: time — Time access and conversions
links.why: Every clock in the time module with the clock it reads: time, monotonic, perf_counter, sleep, ctime, and the rule that maps %y to 1969-2068.

links.title: datetime — Basic date and time types
links.why: The reference for datetime, timedelta, aware and naive values, and the table of strftime and strptime directives.

links.title: subprocess — Subprocess management
links.why: run, CompletedProcess, Popen with poll, wait and kill, and the security considerations for shell=True.

links.title: sched — Event scheduler
links.why: The in-process scheduler: events ordered by time and then priority, with a clock and a delay function you can replace.

links.title: threading — Thread-based parallelism
links.why: Timer objects, which run a function once after a delay and can be cancelled while they wait.

links.title: zoneinfo — IANA time zone support
links.why: Attaching a named time zone to a datetime, and how daylight saving time changes the arithmetic.

links.title: shlex — Simple lexical analysis
links.why: split, quote and join: turning shell-style text into an argument list and quoting text for a shell.

links.title: webbrowser — Convenient web-browser controller
links.why: open, open_new and open_new_tab: showing a page in the default browser.

links.title: PEP 418 – Add monotonic time, performance counter, and process time functions
links.why: Why time.monotonic and time.perf_counter were added: a program that times or schedules with the system clock fails when the clock is set.

links.title: PEP 615 – Support for the IANA Time Zone Database in the Standard Library
links.why: Why the zoneinfo module exists and how it attaches named zones to datetimes.

links.title: Python Tutor
links.why: Paste a program and step through it line by line, for example the stopwatch or the Friday the 13th loop, to see each value change.

_note: Every url was opened with an HTTP request through the session proxy on the date in 'checked' and its page title read; the documentation pages served on that date were headed Python 3.14.8, while the chapter research read the 3.14.4 sources. The strftime.org site that the textbook recommends answered 403 to the request and was not opened, so it is not listed.
